tables.label: Table 1
tables.caption: Key physicochemical parameters of parental and mutant peptides.
footnotes: H, hydrophobicity; µH, hydrophobic moment. Calculated from http://heliquest.ipmc.cnrs.fr/cgi-bin/ComputPararmsV2.py.

tables.label: Table 2
tables.caption: CD data of the peptides.
footnotes: The peptides (150 µM) were dissolved in 10 mM PBS (pH 7.4), 50% TFE, or 30 mM SDS.
The mean residue molar ellipticities [θ]222 (degree•cm2•dmol−1) at wavelength 222 nm were measured at 25°C.
The helical content (%) of a peptide relative to the molar ellipticity value of peptide T9F in 50% TFE.

tables.label: Table 3
tables.caption: Antimicrobial activity and cytotoxic activity of parental and mutant peptides.
footnotes: Minimal inhibitory concentration (MIC) was determined as the lowest concentration of the peptides that inhibited bacteria growth, and minimal bactericidal concentration (MBC) was the concentration resulting in no bacterial growth.
A ciprofloxacin-resistant strain, which MIC for ciprofloxacin was above 512 µM.
A gentamincin-resistant strain, which MIC for gentamincin was above 512 µM.
A ceftazidime-resistant strain, which MIC for ceftazidime was above 512 µM.
HC50 value was taken as the concentration of peptide producing 50% hemolysis.
LD50 value was taken as the concentration of peptide producing 50% cell death.

tables.label: Table 4
tables.caption: MIC values of T9W against P. aeruginosa 27853 in the presence of physiological saltsa.
footnotes: The values represent the MICs of T9W in the absence or presence of salts, and the concentrations of the salts were as follows: 150 mM NaCl, 4.5 mM KCl, 6 µM NH4Cl, 8 µM ZnCl2, 1 mM MgCl2, and 4 µM FeCl3.
